seed_edits.reason: Instantiates #field-ops as a public channel belonging to Northwind Labs, the conversation named in the prompt.
Carlos Vega is the sole conversation-membership record in #field-ops, the join used to identify the candidate user via the route.
Negative alternative: a user with a correct-workspace (Northwind) membership but no #field-ops conversation membership, showing workspace-only matching would be wrong.

Grants the acting user (agent) workspace membership in Northwind Labs so users.info/users.list and conversations discovery for that workspace's public #field-ops channel and user_teams facts are reachable through documented APIs, without altering the fact that Carlos is the sole channel_members row in #field-ops.

notes: The route requires a single user_teams row that simultaneously (a) belongs to team_id=T02NORTHWIND and (b) belongs to a user who is a channel_members row in the Northwind-owned #field-ops channel. Carlos Vega satisfies the conversation-membership leg but his only user_teams row is for Test Workspace (T01WORKSPACE), so scope excludes him. Mateo Rivera satisfies the workspace-membership leg (Northwind) but has no channel_members row in #field-ops, so the focal join excludes him. No user_teams row satisfies both legs, so the selector correctly returns an empty set, matching the 'absent' resolution mode. The acting user (U01AGENBOT9) was given a Northwind Labs workspace membership (not a #field-ops channel membership, preserving Carlos as sole member) so it can use users.info/users.list and conversations.list/members scoped to Northwind Labs to discover the channel's sole member and check for (and fail to find) a corresponding Northwind workspace-membership row, per documented API access. No hidden-table or unsupported-filter access was assumed.
